generation_settings.description: The story's override of the deployment's Lite generation defaults (FR-LITE-4).

guardrail_retry_budget.description:

safe fallback is used (FR-GUARD-6; #68), over the whole turn; ``0`` goes straight to the
fallback. Prospective.

lite_summary_chunk.description: The story's override of the transcript rows per level-0 summary segment (#72).

lite_summary_max_tokens.description: The story's override of the rolling summary's token cap (#72).

lite_window_messages.description:
The story's override of how many transcript rows a Lite prompt keeps verbatim before
older ones are summarised (#72).

max_model_calls_per_turn.description:
The most model calls one turn may make (NFR-PERF-6; #69), 1 to 50. ``None``: the
deployment's default, else the Lite formula ``4 + 5 + G``. A cap below one generation plus

regenerate_retry_budget.description:
How many times a turn whose read set was touched is regenerated before the call fails

turn_concurrency.description:

turn_deadline.description:

deployment's ``turn_queue_max``, default 5); one more is 423 ``story_busy``. Stored in its

EffectivePolicyBody.title: EffectivePolicyBody

RespondRequest.description:
``POST /stories/{id}/respond`` and ``Engine.respond``.

- ``actor_character_id``: whose input this is. Any cast member may act, a player's own
  character or not: who acts is the consumer's call (FR-AUTH-3).
- ``player_input``: the actor's ``say``/``do``; the turn's first beat. It is only ever the
  actor's own speech and action: there is no field for another character's words, and a
  ``say`` that quotes a render character is still the actor speaking (FR-AUTH-3 b).
- ``render_character_ids``: who answers, voiced in this order in one combined reply
  (FR-RESP-5, FR-LITE-5). Omitted: every cast member except the actor, or the actor when
  no one else is in the cast. The actor may be listed. An explicit empty list is refused,
  and duplicates are dropped.
- ``output_viewpoint``: ``character:<id>`` or ``omniscient``; default the actor.
- ``prompt_params``: ``length`` (``short``/``medium``/``long`` or a token cap),
  ``temperature`` and ``top_p``, for this request only (FR-RESP-3).
- ``scene_context``: non-authoritative; never stored or placed in a prompt.
- ``budget``: this turn's ``max_calls``/``deadline_s``, within the story's (#69).

info.description: Epistrel runs behind the consumer and must never be exposed to end users. It authenticates only the calling service, which sends one of the deployment's service credentials as `Authorization: Bearer <credential>`, and it holds no user roles, grants, or permissions: which end user may call which operation, act as which character, or request which output viewpoint is the consumer's decision, made before it calls. Its privacy guarantee is relative to the request: output is produced for the output viewpoint the request names, and Epistrel does not verify that the consumer was entitled to request that viewpoint, so Epistrel by itself does not stop a player from reaching another character's secrets. Every mutating call carries an opaque requesting principal in `X-Epistrel-Principal`, which Epistrel records for attribution and never interprets; use opaque IDs rather than names or email addresses, so recorded attribution identifies no one without your own records.

get.description: The Prometheus text exposition of the engine's metrics: identifiers and counts only, never story content (invariant 3). Served without a credential (invariant 4).

An operation's kind, status (`in_flight`, `committed`, `abandoned` or `failed`), position (`narrative_turn`, `turn_variant`), the story's `timeline_revision` once it committed, the requesting principal, its timestamps, revalidation `attempts`, `config_revisions`, `origin` (`generated` or `ingested`) and, for an ingested batch, `batch_operation_ids`.

A result produced for an output viewpoint (a turn) is returned only when `?viewpoint=` names that viewpoint; another named viewpoint is 409 `idempotency_conflict`. After the window `result` is absent: the operation is the reference a retry receives. Unknown ids are 404.

post.description: Copy the story's corrected history through `at_turn` (default the head) into a new story: every active record positioned at or before it, the cast, settings, rating, pinned memories, custom instructions and story policies, under new ids. The copy reads one snapshot of the source, so it equals the source at exactly one timeline revision (`forked_from.revision`), and the two stories are independent from then on. `variant_chain` (`{turn, variant}` or `"turn:variant"`) copies another chain, e.g. a dormant continuation, as the fork's active history; `at_turn` must then lie on it (422 otherwise), and a chain that names no variant or continues in more than one way is 409 `unknown_chain`. `at_turn` above the head is 422. An archived story can be forked; the fork is active. Answers 201 with `Location`. The source records a `fork` event and keeps its revision. `Idempotency-Key` (per deployment, like story creation) and `X-Epistrel-Expected-Revision` (the source's) are optional.

get.description:
The story's corrected history through `as_of` (default: the latest turn), produced for one **output viewpoint**: `?viewpoint=` (`character:<id>` or `omniscient`), else `?actor_character_id=`, else the story's `default_output_viewpoint`; when none resolves the read is refused (422 `viewpoint_unresolved`). `omniscient` is used only when named.

A character viewpoint never receives `think` or `latent` beats. Under the `lite` profile perception is `none`, so every other beat is returned in full and `audience_filter` is `"none"`: Epistrel does not decide which callers may request which viewpoint. Omniscient items carry the true ages of the characters they name.

`include_audit=1` adds the turns' audit records and requires `viewpoint=omniscient` (403 `omniscient_required`). Pages hold whole turns, newest first, up to `limit` items; pass `next_before_turn` as `before_turn` for the previous page.

`variant=turn:variant` reads along another chain of the story (`GET /stories/{id}/variants`), e.g. a dormant continuation or a regenerated reply's earlier variant: the active history up to where it parts, then that chain's turns; `as_of` defaults to its tip. A chain that names no variant, or continues in more than one way, is 409 `unknown_chain`.

`include_summary=1` adds `summary`: the Lite rolling-summary segments the prompt includes now (wholly at or before `as_of`), oldest first, each `{level, covers_from, covers_to, text, operation_id}`; they are never history items.

post.description:
Record events into the story's authoritative history without generating a reply: a `player_turn` (an actor's `say`/`do`) or consumer-authored `narration` (`text`, no actor). Each event is its own narrative turn at the next turn index and advances the timeline revision; up to 50 events are recorded all or nothing, each through the input gate.

Every event carries a `client_event_id` unique within the story. Re-ingesting an ID with the same payload returns the original result and writes nothing; the same ID with a different payload is 409 `client_event_conflict`. The response is 201 when every event is new and 200 when any was replayed (`Idempotent-Replay: true` when all were). `outcome` and `state_change` events arrive in M6 (422 `unsupported_event_kind`).

The batch is one turn for turn concurrency: while a generated turn runs, a story with `turn_concurrency: reject` answers 423 `story_busy`, and one with `queue` queues the batch (waiting for it up to the story's `turn_deadline`, then 202 `{operation_id, position}`; `Prefer: respond-async` answers 202 at once).

The response reports what the input gate spent: `model_calls` (one `guardrail_check` per model-assisted input policy per text) and `elapsed_ms`.

A latest turn without a reply (an ingested player turn, a narration turn) is 422 `nothing_to_regenerate`. The answer is the respond body plus `previous_variant`. While another turn of the story runs the regenerate is 423 `story_busy` (it is never queued); queued turns fail with `timeline_changed`. `Idempotency-Key` and `X-Epistrel-Expected-Revision` are optional.

post.description:
Play one turn of a story. The request names the acting character (any character of the story; who acts as whom is your decision), what they say and/or do (`player_input`, the turn's first beat and only ever the actor's own words), who answers (`render_character_ids`: default every other character, voiced in the order given and composed into one message), the output viewpoint (`character:<id>` or `omniscient`; default the actor, then the story's default; echoed as `output_viewpoint`, and `beats` are produced for it), prompt parameters (`length`, `temperature`, `top_p`) and optional scene context.

The consumer does no retrieval or memory work: the prompt is assembled from the story's own records. Scene context is checked against the cast and then ignored: it is never stored and never placed in the model's context.

The response is the **finished** reply: under the `lite` profile it is generated in one model call (plus one `guardrail_check` per model-assisted output policy) and none of its claims is checked against the story's facts. Before it is released the reply is checked against the story's output policies: a reply that breaks one is generated again with the policy's message as a constraint, up to the story's `guardrail_retry_budget`, and then the character's safe fallback line is returned instead (`guardrail.fallback_used`, `degradation: ["safe_fallback"]`). Rejected drafts are audit records only. Several characters are voiced in one generation, and their knowledge is kept apart only by instructions in that shared prompt.

Every turn runs under a model-call budget and a deadline: the story's `max_model_calls_per_turn` (default `9 + G`, where G is one call per model-assisted input policy plus one per model-assisted output policy) and `turn_deadline`, or a smaller `budget: {max_calls, deadline_s}` in the request (above the story's is 422). A budget below one generation plus G is refused with 422 `budget_below_safety_minimum` (`details.minimum_required`) before any model call. The response reports `model_calls` (every attempt, failed ones included), `call_counts` by purpose, `elapsed_ms`, `budget` `{max_calls, reserved, used}` and each `degradation` step with its cause; a 503 carries `model_calls` and `elapsed_ms` in `details`.

Optional headers: `Idempotency-Key` (a retry returns the identical response) and `X-Epistrel-Expected-Revision` (a stale revision is refused with 409 and nothing written).

While another turn of the story runs, a story with `turn_concurrency: reject` (the default) answers 423 `story_busy` with `Retry-After`, and one with `queue` queues the turn and plays the queued turns in order, each after the previous one finished. The request waits for its queued turn up to the story's `turn_deadline`, then answers 202 `{operation_id, position}` with `Location: /operations/{id}` while the turn stays queued; `Prefer: respond-async` answers 202 at once. A retry under the same `Idempotency-Key` waits for the same turn. A full queue (`turn_queue_max`) is 423.

patch.description:
Change the story's settings with a JSON merge patch (RFC 7396): a key present sets that setting, `null` resets it to its default, and `generation_settings` merges the same way. `turn_concurrency` (`reject` | `queue`), `turn_queue_max` (1-50; `null`: the deployment's default, 5), `turn_deadline` (seconds), `max_model_calls_per_turn` (1-50; `null`: the deployment's default, else `9 + G`), `default_output_viewpoint` (`character:<id>` of the cast, never `omniscient`), `regenerate_retry_budget` (0-10), `guardrail_retry_budget` (0-5: regenerations after a reply breaks an output policy, before the safe fallback), `generation_settings`, `lite_window_messages`, `lite_summary_chunk` (2-200 rows per summary segment), `lite_summary_max_tokens` (the rolling summary's token cap) and `audit_retention_days` (1-3650; `null`: the deployment's). An unknown key is 422. `policies` (optional) upserts the story's own policies; an item that would relax a policy refuses the whole request with 422 `cannot_relax` before anything is written.

Every setting but `default_output_viewpoint` is prospective: it applies to requests that arrive after the write, never to a turn already running; `default_output_viewpoint` is interpretive (a turn in flight is checked against it when it commits). A write that changes something moves the story's `config_revision`.

post.description:
Make the chain `to_variant_chain` (`{turn, variant}` of its first turn, as `GET /stories/{id}/variants` lists it) active: everything active after the turn where it parts from the active chain becomes `dormant`, and the chain's turns (and the work positioned on them) become `active`. Nothing is deleted; swapping back restores the exact prior state. Swapping to the active chain writes nothing (200, `operation_id` null). A chain that names no variant, or continues in more than one way, is 409 `unknown_chain` (with the `candidates` to choose from). Turns waiting in the story's queue fail with `timeline_changed`.

A control action: it bumps the story's timeline revision, and a turn generating while it commits is abandoned with 409 `timeline_changed`. `Idempotency-Key` and `X-Epistrel-Expected-Revision` are optional.

post.description:
Delete a message and everything after it, without destroying anything: every operation positioned after `to_turn` becomes `discarded` (stamped with this transaction's time); no event is deleted and no valid-time changes, and `untruncate` brings them back. `to_turn` runs from 0 (keep only the story's setup) to the head - 1; anything else is 422. Turns waiting in the story's queue fail with `timeline_changed`.

A control action: it bumps the story's timeline revision, and a turn generating while it commits is abandoned with 409 `timeline_changed`. `Idempotency-Key` and `X-Epistrel-Expected-Revision` are optional.

post.description:
Reactivate exactly what the most recent truncation discarded (undo is last in, first out). Naming `truncate_operation_id` is optional; a truncation that is not the most recent one, or none at all, is 409 `nothing_to_undo` (listing `options: ["swap", "fork"]` and the `dormant_chains` when there are any). When newer turns were written after the truncation, undoing it is a swap: the original continuation becomes active and the newer one dormant, nothing is lost, and the answer says `swapped: true` with the `active_chain`.

A control action: it bumps the story's timeline revision, and a turn generating while it commits is abandoned with 409 `timeline_changed`. `Idempotency-Key` and `X-Epistrel-Expected-Revision` are optional.

get.description: Every chain of the story's variant tree: each turn variant continues the active variant of the turn before it, and a chain is a run of variants continuing one another with the same membership, named by the `{turn, variant}` of its first turn. The `active` chains make up the story; `dormant` ones are continuations a swap can bring back (a regenerated reply, a rewound tail newer turns were written over); `discarded` ones are rewound tails `untruncate` can reactivate.
